final_answer:
All positive solutions are parametrized by a number \(k>0\):

\[
u_k(x)=\log\!\left(\frac{\cosh^2(k/2)}{\cosh^2(k(x-\tfrac12))}\right),
\]

and these solve the boundary value problem exactly when

\[
\lambda=\lambda(k)=\frac{2k^2}{\cosh^2(k/2)}.
\]

The linearized operator has a nontrivial Dirichlet kernel exactly at a turning point of this solution branch, i.e. when

\[
\lambda'(k)=0.
\]

Now

\[
\log \lambda(k)=\log 2+2\log k-2\log\cosh(k/2),
\]

so

\[
\frac{\lambda'(k)}{\lambda(k)}
=\frac{2}{k}-\tanh(k/2).
\]

Thus degeneracy occurs exactly when

\[
k\tanh(k/2)=2.
\]

Let \(a=k/2\). Then the condition is

\[
a\tanh a=1.
\]

This equation has a unique positive solution \(a>0\), since \(a\tanh a\) is strictly increasing from \(0\) to \(\infty\). Therefore the unique degenerate parameter is

\[
\lambda_*=\frac{8a^2}{\cosh^2 a},
\qquad a>0,\quad a\tanh a=1.
\]

Using \(\tanh a=1/a\), one may also write

\[
\lambda_*=8(a^2-1).
\]

So the exact set is

\[
\boxed{\left\{\,8(a^2-1)\;:\; a>0,\ a\tanh a=1\,\right\}}.
\]

Numerically, \(a\approx 1.19968\), so \(\lambda_*\approx 3.5138\).
